description: An interactive workbench for Gauss-Bonnet on a triangle. description: A multi-mode generative biomechanical creature built from GENERATED MESH SURFACES rather than assembled primitives - the non-primitive counterpart to the biomech artifact, for rounder continuous topology. mode selects one of four surface-generation strategies: serpentloft (a rearing serpent whose body is ONE continuous lofted swept tube via MorphoSweep.sweep - a flowing surface no primitive stack can make - with a metal vertebral spine, noise-rippled muscle skin, and a glowing head pod) / fusion (flesh melting into metal as ONE marching-cubes isosurface - MorphoPrimitive.marching_cubes over an sdf_smooth_union field, the flesh-vs-metal seam graded smoothly by a per-vertex shader, with a socketed glow core, eyes and vein cracks) / carapace (a Gielis superformula shell - MorphoPrimitive.superformula_body, the spherical product of two mismatched-symmetry superformulae giving huge organic-mechanical variety - on bezier-swept legs with a sensor head and glow port) / mech (procedural hard-surface armor: inset/extrude raised panels + convex-hull armor chunks + greebles over a revolution shell, deep-red flesh showing through the panel seams). Seed varies the specimen deterministically; the colour triad re-registers the same anatomy between palettes: color_a is the living FLESH (kept deep and saturated - light salmon washes pale under subsurface), color_b is the dark METAL (an emission floor keeps the steel legible), accent is the GLOW. complexity also scales the fusion mode's marching-cubes resolution.

description: A multi-mode generative microorganism after Ernst Haeckel's Kunstformen der Natur - latticed, perforated, radially-symmetric forms built from GENERATED open mesh (struts + nodes), a topology grammar of clusters. mode selects one of four genera: radiolarian (a hollow geodesic LATTICE sphere - a subdivided-icosahedron edge skeleton of ivory struts you see straight through, radial spines bursting outward, a glowing nucleus suspended inside) / cyrtoid (a chambered LATTICE bell - a gourd/amphora of meridian + ring struts in 2-4 constriction chambers, an apical horn, basal spines, a nucleus in the base chamber) / siphonophore (a hanging COLONY cluster - a swept stem hung with a varied series of translucent swimming-bells and glowing bodies, dangling curtains of bezier tentacle clusters: one organism made of many kin units) / diatom (a geometric radial PERFORATED disc/star - concentric ring struts + radial ribs as open areolae cells in strict m-fold symmetry, a spiky star rim, a glowing centre). Seed varies the specimen deterministically; the colour triad re-registers the same anatomy: color_a is the translucent MEMBRANE / protoplasm, color_b is the IVORY skeleton / silica lattice, accent is the bioluminescent NUCLEUS / glow. complexity scales lattice subdivision, chamber/colony/ring counts.

description: A multi-mode generative SURREAL ARCHITECTURE sculpture after Luigi Serafini's Codex Seraphinianus - impossible, anamorphic, morphing arches where building and organism blur, built from NON-PRIMITIVE swept/generated surfaces. mode selects one of eight: arcade (a curving colonnade of repeating masonry arches on columns with a sweeping entablature, warped in reverse perspective) / vault (a ribbed barrel vault tunnel receding into impossible depth - concave coursed interior, transverse and longitudinal ribs, piers, a glowing far throat) / warp (a single hero arch whose span TWISTS and MORPHS - a hand-rolled cross-section morph square-to-diamond plus heavy twist and out-of-plane lean, masonry bent like taffy, a watching keystone-eye) / organic (a rounded vault clad in overlapping living SCALES with a tree and roots growing up through the opening on a diamond-tiled base - architecture fused with creature). Four more (vol.2, grown from Codex reference plates): ribarch (a monumental arch of concentric STRIPED ribbed bands springing from spindly tapered legs, a crown finial at the apex, foam-cells on the ground) / foambridge (a span that is a FOAM/CELLULAR membrane - mostly elliptical holes held by thin struts, jewel-tinted cells, a pendant teardrop) / oculus (a BRICK wall with a great dentil-ringed circular OCULUS, a pointed-arch arcade, a striped toothed column, a blood-red pool with stepping stones) / rainbowspan (a great curving ARC BRIDGE to a terraced HILL-TOWN glittering with warm window-lights). Seed varies the specimen deterministically; the colour triad re-registers it: color_a is the warm MASONRY/stone (or ribarch rib / foam membrane / brick / bridge), color_b is the pale TRIM/rib limestone (or organic green SKIN / ribarch stripe / foam anchor / building walls), accent is the soft warm APERTURE GLOW (or ribarch under-glow / pendant / oculus blood-pool / window-lights). complexity scales bay/rib/twist/cladding detail.

description: A multi-mode generative SURREAL FOOD specimen after Luigi Serafini's Codex Seraphinianus food chapter - everyday edibles fused with mechanism, flame, seed, and the uncanny, built from NON-PRIMITIVE generated surfaces. mode selects one of four: tuber (a lumpy SDF-marching-cubes POTATO fused with brass PLUMBING - pipes, a hand-wheel valve, gauges with needles, a red mushroom-knob valve, a spigot, bolt feet: a vegetable that is secretly a machine) / candleroot (a red RADISH/beet bulb that is a CANDLE - a glowing flame at the crown, white wax drips, green leaves, a root tail on a wax pool) / seedpod (a green GOURD/pepper CUT OPEN - a wedge removed to reveal pale inner flesh packed with a cluster of glowing gold SEEDS on a placenta, stem, spilled seeds) / zipfruit (a purple aubergine UNZIPPING along a zipper seam - two half-shells gaping to reveal a glowing faceted CRYSTAL geode where the flesh should be, a pull-tab). description: A multi-mode generative BOTANICAL specimen - Luigi Serafini's Codex Seraphinianus imaginary-botany rendered as GENUINE L-SYSTEMS, a teaching object for the lsystems curriculum sequence (a sentence becomes a forest; the plant is its rule). mode selects one of four grammars: bracketed (a canonical bracketed L-system tree - axiom + production rules expanded over generations, walked by a 3D turtle with push/pop branch stack and depth decay, a surreal Codex canopy and thread-roots) / helix (a parametric double-helix DNA-ladder stem - two phase-offset helical strands with rungs, golden-angle phyllotaxis leaves, a layered artichoke head with a glowing core) / spacefill (a space-filling Koch L-system curve swept as a recursively-crinkled tendril frond with blooms) / inflorescence (a recursive phyllotactic flowering grammar - a stem rule re-applied over depth, golden-angle branching into size-graded Codex blooms with glowing centers). Seed varies the specimen; the colour triad re-registers it: color_a FOLIAGE/PETAL, color_b WOODY stem/strand, accent BLOOM/FRUIT/core GLOW. complexity scales L-system generations / branch depth / helix turns / bloom count.

description: A multi-mode generative MORPHOGENESIS specimen - Luigi Serafini's Codex Seraphinianus fauna-metamorphosis rendered as GENUINE morphogenesis ALGORITHMS, teaching objects for the cellularautomata / softbodies(reaction-diffusion) / machinelearning(evolution) spine sequences (form is a process; the pattern computes itself). mode selects one of four: lifecycle (a developmental stage-SEQUENCE - egg to larva to pupa to winged adult along an arc, growing, threaded by a glowing progression line) / division (a REAL Conway's Game of Life run on a grid, embodied as a translucent cell colony on a petri-mound: glowing newborns, dumbbell mitosis cells, faded dying husks) / turing (a REAL Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion simulation mapped to a creature's skin as raised teal-rimmed ocelli spots via a ramp - Turing morphogenesis, the hero) / taxon (an evolved-variant taxonomy GRID - egg-pods grown from a mutating genome with a selection cline plus sibling drift). description: A multi-mode generative WRITING-SYSTEM specimen - Luigi Serafini's Codex Seraphinianus asemic script rendered as GENUINE grammar and graph ALGORITHMS, teaching objects for the lsystems and graphtheory spine sequences (the mark is a rule; the page is a graph; writing was always computation). mode selects one of four: glyphgrid (a combinatorial stroke-GRAMMAR - 7 stroke primitives composed by 4 attachment rules into a grid of distinct asemic glyphs in raised relief on a parchment tablet, some gold-rubricated) / branchscript (a REAL bracketed L-SYSTEM - axiom + production rules expanded over generations, a 3D turtle growing a single ornate branching letterform with curling flourishes and illuminated tips) / glyphgraph (REAL GRAPH THEORY - a glyph-node network whose Prim's MINIMUM SPANNING TREE is computed and highlighted as glowing arcs) / codexcolumn (generative cursive - a pen-walk of sine + value-noise + loops + word-gaps swept as raised ink ribbons into lines of flowing asemic script on a parchment stele, with an illuminated initial). description: A multi-mode generative GRID specimen - Luigi Serafini's Codex Seraphinianus board-game, counting and weaving plates rendered as GENUINE array ALGORITHMS, teaching objects for the array_tutorial spine sequence (the grid is the first order: index, modulo, repeat; the loom is a 2D array you can hold). mode selects one of four: weave (a real 2D over-under WEAVE from a boolean pattern matrix - warp and weft interlacing on a loom, a tartan emerging from two crossing colour sequences) / abacus (a real PLACE-VALUE counting array - rods of beads encoding a number in a base, counted beads clustered, highlighted places) / boardtrack (a real GRID-INDEX traversal - a board whose boustrophedon track is row = k//W, col = k%W, with counters, ladder/portal arcs and a glowing finish) / wallpaper (a real WALLPAPER-GROUP tessellation - a motif replicated by a chosen group's symmetry operations using modular arithmetic per cell). description: A multi-mode generative SWARM specimen - Luigi Serafini's Codex Seraphinianus ant-armies, fish-schools and bird-flocks rendered as GENUINE swarm ALGORITHMS run to convergence and frozen as geometry, teaching objects for the swarmintelligence spine sequence (no leader, no plan: local rules make the global shape; intelligence is what the swarm does, not what any agent knows). mode selects one of four: flock (real BOIDS - Reynolds separation / alignment / cohesion stepped to a banking murmuration, every bird oriented along its velocity, leading-edge leaders glowing) / anttrail (real ANT COLONY OPTIMIZATION - elitist ant system over a node graph, pheromone^a*(1/length)^b choice with evaporation, a dominant shortest-path trail emerging glowing with a marching ant column) / shoal (real VICSEK model - self-propelled agents aligning to neighbour-average heading plus noise, frozen as a swirling bait-ball) / pso (real PARTICLE SWARM OPTIMIZATION - particles over a Gaussian fitness landscape funnelling into a glowing global-best attractor with velocity streaks). Seed varies the run; the colour triad re-registers each form: color_a AGENT body, color_b SECONDARY (wing/belly/terrain/weak-edge), accent LEADER / PHEROMONE / glint / ATTRACTOR GLOW. complexity scales agent count and ACO graph size.

description: Hokusai's 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa' rendered as GENUINE algorithm - a deep Prussian-blue wave rearing on the left whose breaking lip is a LOGARITHMIC SPIRAL (r = a*e^(b*theta), the golden-spiral the print is famous for fitting) and whose cascading claw-foam is a RECURSIVE SELF-SIMILAR branching (each foam finger spawns smaller same-curled fingers to a depth set by complexity). A light-blue inner spiral, a foreground swell with its own curl, a small snow-capped Mt Fuji in the gap, all against a cream paper sky. A teaching object / showpiece for the wavefunctions, spirals and fractals strands. description: A 6-bone FABRIK3D tentacle on a pedestal (same IK family as octapod_crawler — steerable by target position). The cycle is: REST_INITIAL (hold upright 10s) → GRAB_UP (first sky reach) → DWELL_PRE → render cube in mid-air → DWELL_POST → DESCEND (carrying cube) → place pyramid → DWELL_PLACE → RISE (clean vertical lift above the just-placed pyramid) → TRANSIT (horizontal traverse at sky height to next placement) → REST → repeat. Wire `placed(index, world_position)` and `rendered(index, world_position)` signals.

Each rod is a DIGIT, the up-beads are the DIGIT VALUE, and the row of digits across the rods is a POSITIONAL NUMBER. By default the up-counts encode π to 7 digits (3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2). In the lab's grammar the abacus is the ALGORITHM OF POSITIONAL NUMERALS — place-value representation as object: rod = position, bead count = digit, rack = number. Portal-orange accent stripe across the bottom rail.

description: A flat rectangular reflective glass pane in a dark wooden frame, optionally on a small base — a looking-glass standing in the lab. Multi-mirror arrangements compose: 'single' (one mirror, identity), 'parallel' (two mirrors facing each other 0.6m apart, infinite reflection cone), 'triangular' (three mirrors arranged as an equilateral triangle viewing inward, the kaleidoscope's parent geometry), or 'rect' (four mirrors arranged as a square, mutual reflection). Portal-orange accent stripe on the bottom of each frame. In the lab's grammar the mirror is the FIXED POINT / IDENTITY OPERATION — the algorithm whose answer is always 'the input again'. Composed with itself in parallel/triangular/rect arrangements, identity generates the dihedral group.

description: A punching bag hanging from a fixed anchor via a cone-twist joint. The cone-twist constraint limits the bag's swing to a 45-degree cone while allowing only 15 degrees of twist — like a ball-and-socket joint with angular limits. Nudge the bag and watch it swing within its invisible cone boundary, then slowly settle as damping absorbs the energy. The joint's bias and softness parameters control how sharply the limits are enforced.

description: A dual-hinge gimbal system with independent yaw and pitch control. Two motor-driven hinges are stacked orthogonally: one rotates freely around the vertical axis (yaw), the other is limited to plus-or-minus 45 degrees on the horizontal axis (pitch). Together they aim a payload in 3D space. The idle mode sweeps smoothly through a Lissajous-like pattern; arrow keys override with direct motor control. This demonstrates how composing multiple single-axis joints creates multi-axis articulation.

description: A motorized crank mechanism combining three joint types into one machine. A hinge joint spins a wheel at constant velocity, a pin joint connects the wheel to a sliding rod, and a slider joint guides the rod along a rail. The result is rotary-to-linear conversion — the fundamental mechanism behind pistons, steam engines, and sewing machines. Watch how continuous rotation becomes reciprocating translation through the geometry of constraint.

description: An interactive Cantor diagonal workbench. One slider drives N ∈ {4, 8, 16, 24, 32}; a list of N random binary reals fills the floating grid, the (i, i) diagonal cells are halo'd in gold, and the bottom row builds the constructed real d bit-by-bit in red — where d[i] = 1 − list[i][i]. Thin orange leaders connect each diagonal cell to its red d-cell, showing 'this bit became that bit, flipped'. The readout reports d's prefix, the 'd ≠ row_k for all k' statement, and the conclusion: the reals are uncountable. description: An interactive Russell's paradox workbench. One slider walks through 6 set definitions ∈ {E, A, C, S, R, Frame}; a translucent disc floats above the plate and redraws to match. For E and C (well-formed predicates) the disc is calm blue with example element dots. For A = {x : x is a set} the disc turns amber and a 'including A itself' tag exposes the self-reference. For S = {x : x ∈ x} it shrinks to a small amber disc with one example dot — consistent self-containment. At cell 5 the disc turns RED with a wavy perimeter, and two orange arrows orbit the disc labeled 'R∈R ⇒ R∉R' and 'R∉R ⇒ R∈R' — chained tip-to-tail into a single closed contradiction loop that spins in space. At cell 6 the disc vanishes and only the loop remains, orbiting a '?'. A consistency lamp on the left glows green / amber / red-blinking by verdict. A ZFC card fades in at cells 5-6 explaining why the axiom of separation foils Russell. Paired with /russell-paradox-gallery — this is the live, hand-cranked version.

description: Six StaticBody3D walls (floor, ceiling, +X, -X, +Z) enclose a 5x5x3 m room; the -Z wall is two side panels + a lintel leaving a 1.2x2.2 m entrance you walk through. An invisible doorway curtain on the ball-only collision layer keeps thrown balls inside while letting the player pass. Balls are RigidBody3D with a bouncy physics material (engine bounces; we visualise). Each ball caches its pre-contact velocity every physics frame; on wall contact it recovers the incident d, looks up the wall's inward normal n̂, computes r = d - 2(d.n̂)n̂, and spawns a ~1.5 s fading d/n̂/r arrow cluster + live formula at the hit point, verifying r against the post-bounce velocity. Fading per-ball trails via ImmediateMesh line strips. A grab-throw ball rack (primary VR) plus an optional ANGLE/FORCE/FIRE console; on desktop/headless the console auto-fires every ~3 s so captures show live bounces. DNA: ball_bounce, gravity_scale, launch_speed, room dimensions.
